clue.text: Exit covers this side?

parts.note: the word Exit wraps round the Roman numeral XI in its middle, and a cricket or football side is a team of that many players

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which side of a building an exit faces.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket and football a side, or team, has this many players; the Roman numeral XI sits inside E-XI-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football team fields this number of players, so a team is commonly called by the number.

clue.text: Left a newspaper unfinished in airport

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the paper's name is cut off

parts.note: the Guardian is a British national daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone left a half-read paper behind at the airport.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York airport is named after Fiorello La Guardia, a former mayor of the city.

clue.text: Old bomb one found in gallery ruin

parts.note: the V-1 was a German flying bomb of the Second World War, written VI with the Roman numeral

indicators.note: found in says the letter for one is placed inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An unexploded wartime bomb is discovered in an art gallery and wrecks it.
explanation.definitionFit: To vitiate something is to spoil or impair it, which is to ruin it.

clue.text: Niece regularly visited and called before wedding?

indicators.note: regularly visited means only every other letter of the word Niece is called on, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A niece made regular visits and phoned ahead of the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: French for born, it introduces a woman's maiden name, the name she was called by before marrying.

clue.text: Returning cheques maybe for deliveries

definitions.meaning: cheques that come back unpaid from the bank are said to bounce
in cricket, short fast balls that rear up at the batsman are known by this name

explanation.surface: A bank's rejected cheques are compared to items being delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler's delivery that is pitched short and rises sharply towards the batsman's head is so called.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a dud cheque and a short-pitched cricket ball are known by this informal term.

clue.text: Jezebel's husband raised one in faith

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the king's name is written upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: in the Bible, Ahab king of Israel was married to Jezebel
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A biblical queen's husband brings someone up in his religion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baha'i faith is a monotheistic religion founded in nineteenth-century Persia.

clue.text: Refined grand finale to include line in popular myth

indicators.note: to include says the string of pieces wraps round the letter for line

parts.note: urbane means suave and refined in manner
G is short for grand, slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
a finale is the end of a show

explanation.surface: A sophisticated, grand ending to a show is made to contain a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts L inside URBANE, between its N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A widely circulated but untrue modern story is what people call this kind of popular myth.

clue.text: Brought round — roughly shaken but not tense

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means roughly or approximately

indicators.note: but not tells us to take away the letter for tense from the word for shaken

parts.note: jolted means shaken by a sudden jerk
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone was revived after being roughly shaken, though not left tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought round' looks like recovering consciousness, but it means persuaded.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone round to your view is to coax or wheedle them into agreement.

clue.text: Rip the centre out of dingy French city

parts.note: a rip is an old word for a dissolute rake, as is a roue

indicators.note: the centre out of means take the middle letter of the five-letter word dingy

explanation.surface: Tearing the heart out of a grubby French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rip' looks like a verb meaning tear, but here it is a noun: a debauched man.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouen is the capital of Normandy in northern France.

clue.text: Set to crack shell, say, get the shakes

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here

indicators.note: shakes says the letters of the words get the are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone prepares to break open a shell, for example, and starts trembling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the shakes' looks like trembling; 'shakes' alone is the anagram signal working on 'get the'. Egg teeth are plural because each hatchling has one, so the set is many.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatching birds and reptiles have a small horny tip on the beak or snout used to break the eggshell.

clue.text: Black girl, posh, wearing nine gemstones

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: wearing says the numeral for nine is worn around the other pieces

parts.note: IX is the Roman numeral for nine
Jo is a girl's name
U stands for upper-class, the posh mark in British usage

explanation.surface: A girl in black, dressed up smartly, decked in nine precious stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Bijoux is French for jewels, used in English for trinkets and gems.

clue.text: Press article about one killer's work

parts.note: to jam is to press or squeeze

indicators.note: about says the article wraps round the following pieces

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
I is the Roman numeral for one
Cain, who killed his brother Abel, is the first killer in the Bible; the 's is the link

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a murderer's handiwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press article' reads as journalism, and 'killer's work' as a crime report, but the definition is just 'work', a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica Inn is a 1936 novel by Daphne du Maurier, a literary work.

clue.text: Horse has been lost, sadly, for a small part of the way

definitions.text: a small part of the way

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters of been lost are put in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: A rider mourns a horse that has gone missing along part of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded stone used in paving makes up one tiny section of a road surface.

clue.text: US city points the way

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
N and E are two compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: An American city shows travellers which way to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A lane is a narrow road or path, a kind of way.

clue.text: Useless, hero could be caught

indicators.note: caught here means heard by the ear, so the word is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: an idol is a hero, someone worshipped

explanation.surface: A useless hero might get caught out.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle threat or gesture is one with no effect, so idle can mean useless.

clue.text: Cobblers showing smoother touch

parts.note: balder, having less hair, means smoother of head
a dash is a small amount, a touch

explanation.surface: Shoemakers are seen applying a lighter finishing touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' looks like shoemakers, but is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobblers is British slang for rubbish talk, the same as balderdash.

clue.text: Time of freedom hasn't guaranteed change in E. Europe

indicators.note: hasn't says the word for guaranteed is missing from the longer word

parts.note: leisure is free time
sure means certain or guaranteed

explanation.surface: A period of liberty has not secured reform in Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like reform, but means coins: lei are the currency units of Romania and Moldova.
explanation.definitionFit: Lei is the plural of leu, the currency of Romania and Moldova, so it is small money there.

clue.text: Wave from comfortable position, concealing Victory sign

indicators.note: concealing says the cushy job hides the sign within it

parts.note: a sinecure is a cushy job needing little work
V, made with two fingers, is the sign for victory

explanation.surface: Someone in a cosy job waves while hiding a V-sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The graph of the sine function is the classic smooth wave in mathematics.

clue.text: Poet —- if I were new I might be — unreadable

indicators.note: might be says the letters could form a different word when rearranged
if I were new means the letter I stands where N would be, so swap N for I

explanation.surface: A poet muses that if he were new he might be unreadable.
explanation.walkthrough: With N standing for 'new', swap the N of UNREADABLE for I and rearrange; the answer and 'unreadable' are anagrams but for that one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Baudelaire was the nineteenth-century French poet of Les Fleurs du mal.

clue.text: Daughter on second drink in masquer-and The ade?

clue.text: Hooter, not for end of work

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word work

explanation.surface: A factory hooter, not meant to mark the end of the working day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' looks like a factory siren, but is slang for the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Conk and hooter are both British slang words for a nose.

clue.text: What to do with partner finding husband in bed with girl?

indicators.note: in places the husband and girl inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Abi is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a husband in bed with a girl and wonders what to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Living together as a couple without being married is what partners do.

clue.text: Area where a team lacks width

indicators.note: lacks says the letter for width is taken away from the word for team

parts.note: a crew is a team, as of rowers

explanation.surface: A field where a team is too narrow to cover the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, about 4,047 square metres.

clue.text: Holiday location has four new clubs Call 0870 opening

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Holiday location has four new clubs Call 0870 opening (5)': stray words from a nearby advert are run into it, the scan is blank and no search gives the printed clue; wordplay C + anagram of FOUR is clear.
annotationWithheld.clue: Holiday location has four new clubs Call 0870 opening

clue.text: Firm attack on King that might put speaker on trial

definitions.text: that might put speaker on trial

parts.note: sound means solid or firm
in chess, check is a direct attack on the king

explanation.surface: A company launches an assault on the monarch that could land an orator in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaker' suggests a person and 'trial' a court, but the speaker is a loudspeaker being tested.
explanation.definitionFit: Before a gig, engineers test the loudspeakers and microphones in a quick trial of the equipment.

clue.text: Ruined, one has broken with German Duke

indicators.note: has broken says the letter for one breaks into the following pieces

parts.note: und is German for and, joining things just as with does
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is ruined after breaking off with a German duke.
explanation.definitionFit: To be undone is to be ruined, so the past tense undid means brought to ruin.

clue.text: Topers moving quickly in bars

indicators.note: moving means the letters of the word Topers change places

explanation.surface: Drinkers hurry along from pub to pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like pubs for the topers, but means bars of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical direction for a very fast tempo, played across the bars of a score.

clue.text: Run in to purchase beads first in town

indicators.note: first says the beads come at the front of the answer

parts.note: dew forms in beads, so beads can be dews

indicators.note: in to says the letter for run goes inside the word for purchase

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone nips into a town to buy beads first.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewsbury is a market town in West Yorkshire, England.

clue.text: Comedian in Carry On, mainly

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, dropping its final letter

parts.note: to wage war is to carry it on

explanation.surface: A comic actor in the Carry On films, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry On' suggests the British film comedy series, but means to wage.
explanation.definitionFit: A wag is a joker or wit, someone who makes people laugh.

clue.text: Elephant stopped after mile — beg for help to get started

indicators.note: stopped after mile means the word is cut short just after its letter M, mile's abbreviation

parts.note: Jumbo was a famous elephant, and the word now names any elephant
to plead is to beg

explanation.surface: An elephant halted after a mile begs for help to get going again.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable connecting two car batteries is used to give a flat engine help in starting.

clue.text: Drew is devastated

definitions.meaning: to draw a chicken is to remove its innards
utterly crushed or very upset, in informal British usage

explanation.surface: A man called Drew is heartbroken.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutted means both disembowelled, as when a cook draws a fowl, and bitterly disappointed.
